teaser.text: Alimentation Couche-Tard runs stores and fuel stations where people quickly buy something for themselves and something for their vehicle. Its business earns money from fuel, convenience goods, prepared food and services, then spends that money on products, people, property and financing.

blocks.heading: Where could Couche-Tard's shares be in October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is C$75.96 in October 2027, a 2% loss including dividends. It reaches C$89.81 in October 2029, an 18% gain. Bear probability is 25%, base probability is 55%, and bull probability is 20%. The base case assumes normalized earnings growth and a P/E near 16x.

The forecast’s central outcome is modest appreciation, but the possible range remains wide. The weighted price is C$75.96 in October 2027, C$81.58 in October 2028 and C$89.81 in October 2029, equivalent to returns including dividends of negative 2%, positive 6% and positive 18%. The 2029 outcomes range from C$50.44 in the bear case to C$130.19 in the bull case, against today’s C$78.64.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Couche-Tard, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case reaches US$2,816 million as revenue grows to US$88,000 million but margin falls to 3.20%. Fuel-margin normalization, weaker volumes and Żabka financing explain the deterioration. The bull case reaches US$3,990 million on US$95,000 million of revenue and a 4.20% margin, requiring foodservice, distribution savings and integration benefits to arrive together. Management targets adjusted EBITDA growth of 6% to 8% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of at least 10%, but that guidance excludes transactions that materially change the portfolio.

blocks.heading: How much does Couche-Tard pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise in the base case from US$0.66 to US$0.80 per share, using roughly 10% annual growth from the latest annualized rate of about US$0.60. That is below the prior five-year growth rate, but fiscal 2026 dividends used only about one fifth of free cash flow. The bear case holds dividends at US$0.60 because debt and investment take priority. The bull case reaches US$0.92 on 15% annual growth, requiring stronger cash earnings and acquisition synergies.

blocks.heading: What has Couche-Tard guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: On February 11, 2026, Couche-Tard introduced Core + More, replacing its earlier outlook. “Core” means improving the businesses it already knows; “More” means adding growth opportunities and the capabilities to support them. Through fiscal 2030, management targets annualized adjusted EBITDA growth of 6.0%–8.0% and adjusted earnings-per-share growth of at least 10.0%, excluding major transactions.

The operating targets are comparable-store merchandise growth of 2%–3%, total merchandise and service revenue growth of 4%–5%, fuel gross profit growth with inflation, and normalized expenses at inflation or below. Comparable-store growth shows whether established locations are improving, rather than letting new stores do all the work.

blocks.heading: Did Couche-Tard keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Promises also need exact definitions. In March 2026, Alex Miller said the company was on track to build 100 new stores by fiscal year-end. The annual report later described 130 sites added or improved, including relocations and rebuilds. Those categories are not interchangeable, so the larger figure does not alone prove the new-build promise was met.

blocks.heading: What do Couche-Tard's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Operating income rose to US$1,223.7 million, while net income reached US$828.5 million. Adjusted net income rose from US$737.0 million to US$827.0 million, showing that the improvement was stronger after removing the prior-year GetGo gain. Fewer shares also helped diluted EPS reach US$0.90.
